title: missing-metric-propagation-and-exporter-rollback-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a fast, informal post-incident scratchpad describing a recurring class of missing-metric incidents where a downstream metrics exporter rollback/upgrade causes partial metric propagation failures across the telemetry pipeline. Goal: capture the triage checklist, short-term mitigations we used, hypotheses we validated/ruled out, and a concise list of follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Symptoms: sudden disappearance of >1 custom business / SLO metrics in dashboards and alerting rules over ~10-30 minutes, while infrastructure-level metrics (host CPU, mem) stayed healthy.
- Root trigger: partial rollback of exporter binary (v2.11 -> v2.10) during a canary that included a config flag change. New/changed metric labels were dropped by v2.10, causing metric families to be rewritten and a propagation gap in remote_write (Thanos/Prometheus federation).
- Impact: SLO burn alerts (customer-facing route latency SLO) triggered noisy pagers and created investigation drag for oncall.
- Short-term fix: pinned exporter to last-known-good, re-triggered metric backfill job, and added a temporary mute for affected SLO alerts while verifying metric recovery.

Incident timeline (notes from oncall):
- 2024-10-03 09:23 UTC: First pager for high SLO burn on /api/generate-route.
- 09:26 UTC: Dashboard shows zero values for metrics: synth_route_latency_bucket and batch_request_success_total (both custom). Node/infra metrics ok.
- 09:30 UTC: Confirmed remote_write still accepting samples (via Prometheus tsdb status).
- 09:37 UTC: Slack thread: exporter-team alerted to recent deploys. Found automated canary rollback executed ~09:15 for exporter v2.11 -> v2.10 in region us-west-2.
- 09:45 UTC: Manual revert to v2.11 on all exporter nodes. Metrics reappeared gradually 09:50-10:05 as federation resumed accepting matched metric families.
- 10:20 UTC: Alerts unmuted after verifying 30 min of stable metrics and corrected label sets.

Triage checklist (quick runbook to run in parallel):
1) Confirm missing-ness: Check metric presence in local Prometheus scrape vs. remote store (use PromQL: count_over_time(metric[5m]) and promtool snapshot).
2) Check exporter status: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=metrics-exporter -o wide and kubectl logs for restarts/args.
3) Inspect exporter version: kubectl exec curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | head -n 5 or check /version endpoint (if present).
4) Review recent deploys: gitlab/github actions + deploy pipeline window; check canary/rollforward logs.
5) Validate federation/remote_write: tail Prometheus logs for dropped samples or label mismatch warnings.
6) If remote store shows mismatched metric families (labels missing/new), suspect exporter/agent change.
7) If needed, rollback exporter to last-known-good and force rescrape/restart.

Diagnostic commands (use carefully in prod):
- PromQL presence check: count_over_time(synth_route_latency_bucket[10m])
- List exporter pods: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=metrics-exporter -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
- Check exporter version via endpoint: kubectl exec -n monitoring <pod> -- curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | head -n 20 | grep -i version -A1
- Look for dropped samples in Prometheus: grep -i "dropped" /var/log/prometheus/prometheus.log || journalctl -u prometheus | tail -n 200
- Check federation rejected series: query Thanos/remote write metrics like "thanos_receive_dropped_samples_total"

Validated hypotheses during incident:
- Hypothesis A: Scraping failure due to node network issue — ruled out (node metrics present, exporter pods healthy).
- Hypothesis B: Aggregation/ingest pipeline outage — ruled out (remote_write healthy, no retention issues).
- Hypothesis C: Exporter backward-incompatible change removed label(s) -> series identity changed -> remote store considered them new series and older series gap triggered alerts — validated (version mismatch & config flag present in release notes).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Reverted exporter to v2.11 on all canary/production pods (manual deploy).
- Triggered re-scrape by restarting one representative exporter pod per AZ to push fresh series metadata.
- Added temporary alert mute for affected SLO rules (15–30 min windows) to prevent pager storms while verifying fixes.

Post-incident follow-ups (short-term):
- SRE-4123: Add a pre-deploy check that compares metric family names/label sets for canary vs baseline before rolling out exporter changes. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Implement a synthetic "exporter_liveness_metric" that is pushed with stable metric name and fixed label set per AZ so we can detect series identity flips (and alert on family churn). Owner: Benjy. ETA: 1 week.
- Update runbook to include explicit "label-set-drift" checks (PromQL snippets) and automated detection via a CI job. Owner: Rina. ETA: 3 weeks.

Longer-term proposals (ideas discussed in postmortem):
- Deploy a metric-schema CI gate in exporter repo that runs against a fixture prometheus/remote_write stack and fails builds that remove or rename metric families without explicit opt-in and migration plan.
- Add a remote_write compatibility layer in the exporter that preserves older label keys for a deprecation window and emits a deprecation counter when new label values are introduced.
- Create a lightweight index of metric families and last-seen checksum stored in the control plane; if a deployment changes checksum significantly, block rollout or require SRE approval.

Pager-noise minimization pattern (operational rules):
- If metrics vanish but infra metrics ok: treat as "telemetry identity churn" — mute noisy SLO alerts for a predefined short window (documented), perform exporter/version check first before large-scale oncall escalation.
- Prefer mute + regional isolation + targeted rollback over system-wide silence.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the canary pipeline allow a rollback from v2.11 -> v2.10 without metric-diff validation? (pipeline gap).
- Do we want to decouple SLO alerting to use synthetic heartbeat metrics in addition to business metrics for baseline health?

Action items for the next retro:
- Walkthrough of the exporter change that triggered this to identify specific missing step in CI gating. (Dev/Infra owners invited.)
- Decide on default mute policy for missing-metric incidents (duration, who can apply, audit trail).
- Draft a short playbook card to be added to the SRE runbook deck: "If business metrics disappear but infra looks fine" (1 pager).

Notes to self / oncall memory aids:
- Always check exporter version & recently deployed Git SHA before paging broader teams.
- Use temporary mute instead of broad paging escalation when evidence points to telemetry changes.
- Keep a pinned link to metric-schema CI in the exporter repo in the runbook once gated.

End of notes.
